Target-model traces therefore have to be generated with the target model itself (API or served checkpoint) on non-benchmark repositories; this remains blocked until access is provided.

CoT portability is measured, not assumed: with harness and task sources fixed, reasoning-channel volume is model- and version-specific (DeepSeek-V4-Flash 44.3k chars/traj with ~12 visible chars, Qwen3.6-27B 0 chars in the same config, Qwen3.8-27B 100.7k chars in the same harness as Qwen3.6, MiniMax-M2.5 24.0k chars). See docs/MICRO-GENERATOR-COT-PORTABILITY-2026-10-07.md.

Correction (2026-10-07, after task clarification): the goal is NOT a model-agnostic progress summary. The micro-compiler takes ONE born reasoning block (raw) plus the context visible at that moment and emits the compressed reasoning block that the TARGET model itself will read back on later turns. Quality is therefore defined downstream, by the target model's continuation performance (gold axes E1/E2: fixedAtRound and vsRaw on the real machine), not by surface similarity to any summary format. Other-model traces can only supply raw material; every compression candidate must be judged with the target model as the reader.
